svg.text: Basal Ganglia: Direct, Indirect and Hyperdirect Pathways
Green = excitatory (glutamatergic, arrowhead) · Red = inhibitory (GABAergic, bar terminal) · Purple = dopaminergic modulation
C · Three canonical routes through the circuit
Output falls in affected channels → downstream
targets are disinhibited and gain influence.
Output rises through the GPe→STN route →
Cortex drives STN rapidly → output can rise
quickly, transiently delaying or suppressing action.
Conduction delays, not just anatomy, order the routes.

• GPe is heterogeneous, not a relay. Prototypic

• Motor, associative and limbic loops run in

DIRECT — decreases output in affected channels
Striatal inhibition lowers firing in the affected
output channel. Thalamic and brainstem targets
influence. Direct and indirect SPNs can be
Striatal inhibition reduces GPe activity; STN is
released and excites the output nuclei. Output
therefore rises in affected channels, increasing
inhibition of downstream targets and reducing
HYPERDIRECT — rapid cortical drive to STN
Cortex excites STN without a striatal step, so
output-nucleus activity can rise rapidly. This can
transiently strengthen inhibition of thalamic and
brainstem targets, delaying or suppressing action
Canonical human/mammalian circuit scaffold; modern refinements are labeled by evidentiary species. Line colour encodes synaptic sign. Not all known connections are shown.
